answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to staked, verifiable compute: each agent must lock real resources and burn a small fee before it may transact, with that commitment recorded on-chain. Spawning thousands of fake personas then costs thousands of times more than one honest agent would ever pay, so impersonation collapses under its own economics. Reputation compounds from that first deposit the way a cedar adds rings, its umber heartwood darkening with age, while genuine demand keeps the network's pulse steady and unbroken.
